$comment: The generator exam (standing backlog 9, D-552): sixty questions a generated pack must answer, each mapped to a lint or a fixture assertion with the official source beside it. Runs over the replayed sole-trader pack in CI (no model call) and over a live pack on the monthly workflow or by hand. mustPass true blocks a prompt-version bump when it fails; mustPass false is reported (a known gap in the recorded replies, with the note saying which recording group fixes it, or a gap in the fixed text for the PO). The NDIS watch adds a question when a rule changes and names the watch change id. {{tradingName}} is replaced with the pack's trading name.

questions.question: A reportable incident is notified to the Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.

values: Within 24 hours of becoming aware (Incident Rules s 20)

source.title: NDIS (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018, s 20

questions.question: The full report of a reportable incident follows within 5 business days.

values: with the full report within 5 business days

questions.question: An unauthorised restrictive practice is notified within 5 business days, in writing.

values: Within 5 business days, in writing (Incident Rules s 21)

questions.question: Reportable incident records are kept for 7 years from the notification.

values: 7 years from the date we notified the Commission
Incident Rules s 25(2)

questions.mapsTo: fixed text: retention-schedule (watch item 4; batch 45 item 18 made the table fixed and sourced)
questions.note: Gap found by the exam on 14 Oct 2026: the retention schedule was a tailored section, so the fixed row never rendered. Batch 45 item 18 (15 Oct 2026) made the section fixed, with a sourced table; must pass from then on.

questions.question: Every policy says it is reviewed every 12 months.

values: We review this document every 12 months

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards, Governance and operational management (quality management)

questions.question: Every document carries its next review date.
questions.mapsTo: fixed text: document control table (REQ-016 S-2)

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards, Governance and operational management (quality management)

questions.question: A worker screening renewal starts at least 90 days before the clearance expires.

values: at least 90 days before the clearance expires

source.title: NDIS Commission, FAQs: NDIS Worker Screening Check renewal cycle (January 2026)

questions.question: A worker whose clearance has expired stops risk-assessed work that day.

values: the worker stops risk-assessed work that day until a new clearance is issued

source.title: NDIS Commission, FAQs: NDIS Worker Screening Check renewal cycle (January 2026)

questions.question: No tailored section restates a statutory time frame; the fixed escalation table is the single source.
The support plan is reviewed at least every 12 months, or sooner when needs change.

values: review it at least every 12 months, or sooner when their needs change

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards, Provision of supports (support planning)

questions.question: The reportable incident categories are named in full.

values: death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact, sexual misconduct

questions.question: The five kinds of restrictive practice are named: seclusion, chemical, mechanical, physical and environmental.

values: seclusion
chemical
mechanical
physical
environmental

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards, Implementing behaviour support plans module

questions.question: A risk-assessed role is defined where worker screening is explained.
questions.mapsTo: fixture: the worker screening procedure's roles section (recording plan group 3)
questions.note: The fixed definitions do not define a risk-assessed role; the tailored roles section names it when recorded. PO: decide whether the fixed definitions should carry it, with the Worker Screening Rules as the source.

questions.question: Key personnel are defined.

values: Key personnel: the people who own, run or make decisions for the business.

questions.question: A participant is defined.

values: Participant: a person who receives supports from us under the NDIS.

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators

questions.question: A worker is defined to include the owner, employees, contractors and volunteers.

values: Worker: anyone who delivers or supports the delivery of our services, including the owner, people we employ, contractors and volunteers.

source.title: NDIS Commission, worker screening (who is a worker)

questions.question: A restrictive practice is defined before the five kinds are listed.

values: A restrictive practice is anything that limits a person's rights or freedom of movement.

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards, Implementing behaviour support plans module

questions.question: The Commission is defined as the body that registers and regulates providers.

values: The Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, which registers and regulates providers.

questions.question: The regulator is named in full as the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.

values: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

questions.question: The regulator is never misnamed.

check.pattern: NDIS Safeguards Commission|Quality and Safeguarding Commission|NDIS Quality Commission|NDIS Safeguarding Commission

questions.question: The auditor is an approved quality auditor, never a certifier or an assessor.
If the accreditor is named, it is JAS-ANZ, spelt that way.
The Code is named as the NDIS Code of Conduct.

values: NDIS Code of Conduct

source.title: NDIS Commission, NDIS Code of Conduct

questions.question: The standards are named as the NDIS Practice Standards.

values: NDIS Practice Standards

source.title: NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators

questions.question: Registration and audits are never attributed to the NDIA.

check.pattern: NDIA registers|registered with the NDIA|NDIA audit|audited by the NDIA|the Agency registers

unlinks workers who leave

questions.question: The pack never says a clearance lasts longer than five years.

check.pattern: clearance (is valid|lasts) for (ten|10|seven|7|six|6) years|clearance does not expire|clearance never expires

source.title: NDIS Commission, FAQs: NDIS Worker Screening Check renewal cycle (January 2026)

questions.note: Not applicable to the sole-trader pack; applies to a live run on the behaviour-support case.
